usage: Regular -are verb: to call someone (by phone or by name). The reflexive chiamarsi means 'to be called'. Common collocations: chiamare un taxi, chiamare aiuto.

examples.en: I'll call you tonight.
I called the doctor yesterday.

examples.it: Chiamerò un taxi per andare in stazione.
examples.en: I will call a taxi to go to the station.

usage: Regular -ere verb, the opposite of comprare. Note the sign 'vendesi' (for sale). Passato remoto: vendei/vendetti.

examples.en: I'm selling my old bike.

examples.it: Hanno venduto la casa in un mese.
examples.en: They sold the house in a month.

examples.it: Se vendessi la macchina, avrei più soldi.
examples.en: If I sold the car, I would have more money.

usage: Irregular participle speso, passato remoto spesi. Commonly used for money, but also for resources such as time, energy and words. For spending a period of time somewhere or doing something, passare or trascorrere is usually more natural. Spendere un occhio della testa means to pay a fortune.

examples.it: Quanto spendi al mese per l'affitto?
examples.en: How much do you spend a month on rent?
We spent too much on holiday.

examples.it: Non spenderò più di venti euro.
examples.en: I won't spend more than twenty euros.

usage: Regular -are verb: preparare la cena, preparare l'esame, preparare la valigia. The reflexive prepararsi means to get ready.

examples.en: I make breakfast for everyone.
Have you packed your suitcase?
Tomorrow we will make a cake.

usage: Regular -are verb. More formal than 'far vedere', which is what people say in conversation: 'ti faccio vedere' = let me show you.

examples.it: Mi mostri il passaporto, per favore?
examples.en: Will you show me your passport, please?

examples.it: Ci ha mostrato le foto del viaggio.
examples.en: He showed us the photos from the trip.
I'll show you the way.

en: to touch; to be someone's turn
usage: Spelling change: tocchi, tocchiamo, toccherò. Touching a direct object uses avere: 'ho toccato il muro'. With an indirect object, toccare can mean being someone's turn or having to do something: 'tocca a me', 'mi è toccato lavorare'. That construction uses essere and its grammatical subject is the turn, task or thing allotted, not the person affected. The reference form table includes both constructions.

examples.en: Don't touch the painting!

examples.it: A chi tocca? Tocca a te.
examples.en: Whose turn is it? It's your turn.

examples.it: Mi è toccato pagare per tutti.
examples.en: I ended up having to pay for everyone.

usage: Regular -are verb; takes a direct object (sognare una casa) or di + infinitive (sogno di viaggiare). Noi form: sogniamo. 'Sognare a occhi aperti' = to daydream.

examples.en: I dream of living in Italy.
Last night I dreamed of the sea.

examples.it: Da bambina sognava di fare la cantante.
examples.en: As a child she dreamed of being a singer.

usage: Regular -are verb. Auxiliary essere when a destination or movement is emphasised (sono volato a Roma), avere for the activity (ha volato per due ore). Also 'il tempo vola' (time flies).

examples.en: Tomorrow I fly to Milan.
Time flew!

examples.it: Ha volato per la prima volta a dieci anni.
examples.en: He flew for the first time at ten.

usage: Stressed -iare verb: the tu form is invii and the noi form inviamo. Slightly more formal than mandare; standard for e-mails and messages (inviare un messaggio).

examples.en: I'll send you the document right away.
I sent the application yesterday.

examples.it: Invii pure la mail quando vuole.
examples.en: Feel free to send the email whenever you like.

usage: Regular -are verb. Guadagnarsi da vivere = to earn a living; guadagnare tempo = to save time.

examples.en: How much do you earn a month?

examples.it: Ha guadagnato molto con quel lavoro.
examples.en: He earned a lot with that job.
That way we'll gain an hour.

usage: Regular -are verb; with che it normally takes the subjunctive when expressing a supposition (immagino che sia stanco). 'Immagino!' = I can imagine!

examples.en: I imagine you are tired.

examples.it: Non avrei mai immaginato una cosa simile.
examples.en: I would never have imagined such a thing.

examples.it: Immagina di essere su una spiaggia.
examples.en: Imagine you are on a beach.

usage: Conjugated like scrivere: participle descritto, passato remoto descrissi.

examples.en: Describe your city.

examples.it: Mi ha descritto la casa nei dettagli.
examples.en: She described the house to me in detail.

examples.it: Vorrei che descrivessi meglio il problema.
examples.en: I'd like you to describe the problem better.

usage: Impersonal weather verb, used in the third person: piove, pioveva, pioverà, è/ha piovuto (both auxiliaries are accepted). Passato remoto: piovve.

examples.en: Today it's raining all day.
Yesterday it poured.
If it rains, we'll stay home.

usage: Impersonal weather verb used in the third person; spelling change nevicherà. Either auxiliary in compound tenses (è/ha nevicato).

examples.en: In the mountains it often snows.
It snowed last night.

examples.it: Domani nevicherà su tutto il nord.
examples.en: Tomorrow it will snow all over the north.

usage: Irregular: participle mosso, passato remoto mossi. The reflexive muoversi means to move (oneself) or to hurry up: 'Muoviti!' = Hurry up! For changing house use traslocare.

examples.en: Don't move your head.
Hurry up, we're late!

examples.it: Non si è mosso dal divano tutto il giorno.
examples.en: He hasn't moved from the sofa all day.

usage: Pronominal verb built on andare with the clitics se + ne: me ne vado, te ne vai, se ne va, ce ne andiamo, ve ne andate, se ne vanno. Imperative: vattene! Passato prossimo: me ne sono andato/a. Very common in speech for 'to leave'.

examples.it: Me ne vado, ci vediamo domani.
examples.en: I'm off, see you tomorrow.

examples.it: Se ne sono andati senza salutare.
examples.en: They left without saying goodbye.
Go away, I don't want to see you!

en: to take (time, effort); to be needed
usage: Impersonal pronominal verb: ci vuole (singular) / ci vogliono (plural) agrees with the thing needed: ci vuole un'ora, ci vogliono due ore. Compound tenses take essere: ci è voluto un anno. Compare metterci (personal subject).

examples.en: It takes an hour to get there.

examples.it: Ci vogliono tre uova per la torta.
examples.en: Three eggs are needed for the cake.
It took a lot of patience.

usage: Pronominal verb with ci: the subject is the person: ci metto dieci minuti (it takes me ten minutes). Compound tenses take avere: ci ho messo un'ora. Also 'mettercela tutta' = to give it one's all.

examples.en: How long does it take you to get here?

examples.it: Ci ho messo due ore a finire.
examples.en: It took me two hours to finish.
It won't take us long, promise.

en: to manage; to make it; to cope
usage: Pronominal verb built on fare with ce + la: ce la faccio, ce la fai, ce la fa… Compound tenses: ce l'ho fatta (the participle is always fatta). 'Non ce la faccio più' = I can't take it any more.

examples.it: Ce la fai a portare la valigia?
examples.en: Can you manage to carry the suitcase?
We made it!

examples.it: Non ce la farò mai in tempo.
examples.en: I'll never make it in time.

en: to have to do with; to be relevant
usage: Pronominal verb with ci, usually in the third person: 'Che c'entra?' (what's that got to do with it?), 'non c'entra niente' (it has nothing to do with it). In speech the ci elides: c'entra, c'entrano.

examples.it: Cosa c'entra questo con il lavoro?
examples.en: What does this have to do with work?
It has nothing to do with me!

examples.it: Non c'è entrato per niente in quella storia.
examples.en: He had nothing at all to do with that business.

usage: For everyday impersonal necessity, use third-person singular: bisogna + infinitive ('bisogna partire presto') or bisogna che + subjunctive. This construction has no personal subject. Its compound participle is masculine singular ('è bisognato partire'), without agreement with the person affected. Rare personal third-person singular/plural uses also exist, but are separate from the common impersonal construction taught here. For 'I need', say 'ho bisogno di'.

examples.en: You have to book in advance.
It should have been said earlier.

examples.it: Bisogna che tu venga con noi.
examples.en: You need to come with us.

usage: Regular -are verb with spelling change (litighi, litigheremo). For a legal dispute use fare causa; for a physical fight, azzuffarsi or picchiarsi.

examples.en: They always argue about money.
I argued with my sister.
Let's not argue in front of the children.

usage: Regular -are verb, informal: to chat, make small talk. 'Fare due chiacchiere' = to have a chat. Chiacchierone = chatterbox.

examples.en: We chatted for hours.
He chats too much during lessons.
They used to chat at the bar every morning.

usage: Regular -are verb. Bisbigliare is a near-synonym; sussurrare is slightly more literary and also used for wind, leaves and water.

examples.en: She whispered something in my ear.

examples.it: Sussurrano per non svegliare il bambino.
examples.en: They whisper so as not to wake the baby.

examples.it: Il vento sussurrava tra gli alberi.
examples.en: The wind whispered through the trees.

en: to lead; to conduct; to drive
usage: Irregular -urre verb (from Latin ducere): conduco, conducevo, condussi, condotto, condurrò. Also 'to host' a TV show (condurre una trasmissione) and 'to lead' a life.

examples.en: She hosts a radio programme.
The investigations led to the arrest.
He led a quiet life.

usage: Conjugated like trarre: attraggo, attrai, attrae… participle attratto, passato remoto attrassi, future attrarrò.

examples.it: La città attrae milioni di turisti.
examples.en: The city attracts millions of tourists.

examples.it: Sono sempre stato attratto dalla musica.
examples.en: I have always been attracted to music.

examples.it: Il nuovo museo attrarrà molti visitatori.
examples.en: The new museum will attract many visitors.

usage: Conjugated like trarre: distraggo, distrai… participle distratto, passato remoto distrassi. The reflexive distrarsi means to get distracted or to take one's mind off things.

examples.en: The noise distracts me.
I got distracted for a moment.

examples.it: Ho bisogno di distrarmi un po'.
examples.en: I need to take my mind off things a bit.

usage: Regular -are verb. Also 'to reckon' or 'to take into account' (non avevo calcolato il traffico).

examples.en: Work out how much it will cost us.
I hadn't reckoned with the traffic.

examples.it: Calcolo di arrivare verso le otto.
examples.en: I reckon I'll arrive around eight.

usage: -isc- verb: diminuisco. Auxiliary essere when intransitive (i prezzi sono diminuiti), avere when transitive (hanno diminuito i prezzi). Opposite: aumentare.

examples.it: I prezzi sono diminuiti del dieci per cento.
examples.en: Prices have fallen by ten per cent.
We have to reduce expenses.
The noise decreases at night.

usage: Regular -are verb borrowed from English, used for social media. Informal but very common; pubblicare is the neutral alternative.

examples.it: Ha postato una foto del tramonto.
examples.en: She posted a photo of the sunset.
Don't post anything without asking me.
We'll post the video tomorrow.

usage: Colloquial recent borrowing (also written guglare); regular -are verb. Neutral alternative: cercare su internet.

examples.en: I don't know, google it.

examples.it: Ho googlato il ristorante prima di prenotare.
examples.en: I googled the restaurant before booking.

examples.it: Se googli il suo nome trovi tutto.
examples.en: If you google his name you'll find everything.
